source_notes: Patterns distilled from the official SceneCode project gallery and repository examples.
SceneCode produces the static executable scene; PyBullet adds certified robot motion and dynamics.

profiles.brief: A Franka Panda picks up one blue ceramic cup from a realistic wooden worktable and places it upright inside one shallow blue tray.

activity_zones: one central wooden manipulation table with a clear robot approach edge
one restrained storage and charging area along the far wall

objects.name: full-size rectangular wooden worktable
objects.placement: centered with clear floor space on all sides and no crossbar blocking the robot base

objects.name: Franka Panda work zone
objects.support: the near edge of the worktable
objects.placement: with unobstructed reach to the cup and tray; reserve space but leave the actual robot to the simulator

objects.name: blue ceramic cup
objects.placement: upright in the front-right manipulation area, 35 cm outside the tray, with side and top grasp clearance

objects.name: shallow blue rectangular tray
objects.placement: left of the cup with its complete interior visible and enough clearance for an upright placement

objects.name: low closed storage cabinet
objects.placement: against the far wall outside the robot and camera paths

objects.name: small charging dock
objects.placement: neatly placed as restrained real laboratory context

wall_and_ceiling: one diffuse side window with a fabric blind
lighting_and_materials: soft daylight plus broad warm-white overhead illumination
matte wood, pale walls, and neutral flooring with realistic contact shadows
enough blue-value contrast to distinguish cup from tray
spec.task_setup: Keep the initial state task-ready but not complete: the cup starts upright outside the tray, the tray interior is empty, and both are visible, reachable, and physically separated
camera_readability: make the cup and tray large enough for reliable video tracking
preserve the complete table task area and robot reach without severe foreshortening
keep fixed-camera silhouettes distinct and leave realistic room context
negative_constraints: tiny task objects, glass, mirrors, glossy black materials, transparent containers, printed text, random clutter
occlusion between cup and tray, intersecting geometry, a pre-solved task, or a robot baked into SceneCode

profiles.brief: A realistic domestic robotics workcell supporting block pick-and-place, target-zone pushing, cup tipping, and stacked-block interaction.

spec.room_type: apartment dining room adapted as a home-robotics workspace
activity_zones: a central manipulation worktable with clear access from the near side
a compact storage and charging zone along the far wall

objects.name: solid rectangular oak worktable
objects.placement: centered in the room with a 1.2 m clear aisle on the near side and no lower crossbar blocking a robot base

objects.name: seven-degree-of-freedom robot work zone
objects.support: a rigid low pedestal aligned with the near edge of the oak worktable
objects.placement: with unobstructed reach to the full tabletop; leave the actual certified robot asset and pedestal to the simulator

objects.name: small red sorting block
objects.placement: in the left-front work area, 20 cm to the left of a shallow blue sorting tray, with clear top and side gripper approach space

objects.name: shallow blue sorting tray and flat green push target pad
objects.placement: with the tray immediately to the right of the red sorting block and the green pad to the right of the wooden manipulation block

objects.name: blue ceramic mug
objects.placement: upright near the center-rear area with its handle visible from the near side

objects.name: rectangular beech manipulation block
objects.placement: near the right-front quadrant with a clear 30 cm sliding path into the green target pad

objects.name: wooden manipulation cubes
objects.placement: in the right-rear quadrant as a stable vertical stack with the middle cube visible from the near side

objects.name: low oak storage cabinet
objects.placement: against the far wall without intersecting the worktable clearance

objects.name: small charging dock and two labeled-free storage bins
objects.placement: neatly grouped as believable robotics-workspace context

wall_and_ceiling: one large window on the left wall with a simple fabric blind
one abstract framed print on the far wall
two warm-white pendant lights centered above the worktable
lighting_and_materials: soft daylight from the left window plus practical warm overhead light
matte oak, pale plaster walls, and a neutral non-gloss floor
distinct saturated colors only for the manipulation targets
spec.task_setup: Keep the initial state task-ready but not complete: the red block begins outside the blue tray with enough clearance to grasp, lift, transfer, place, and release it; the wooden block begins outside the green target pad, the cup is upright, and the three-block stack is stable; every target is separately visible and reachable
camera_readability: keep the full worktable and robot reach zone visible from one fixed oblique near-side view
avoid target overlap and preserve clear silhouettes against the tabletop
leave enough background context to read the room as realistic rather than as an isolated asset showcase
negative_constraints: glass furniture, mirrors, glossy black surfaces, and transparent containers
random clutter, printed text, exposed cables, and objects floating or intersecting
a pre-solved manipulation task or a robot baked into SceneCode geometry

profiles.brief: A realistic cabinet-and-drawer robotics scene for articulated interaction.

objects.name: waist-height wooden cabinet with one drawer and two doors
objects.placement: against the far wall with handles facing the open aisle

objects.name: seven-degree-of-freedom robot work zone
objects.support: the floor across from the cabinet
objects.placement: with a direct unobstructed reach corridor to every handle; leave the certified robot asset to the simulator

objects.name: blue ceramic cup
objects.placement: near the left side and visible from the aisle

objects.name: red wooden block
objects.placement: inside the drawer but not at the final retrieval location

objects.name: woven laundry basket
objects.placement: in the rear-left corner outside robot clearance

objects.name: narrow wall shelf with folded towels
objects.placement: on the right wall above waist height

wall_and_ceiling: a small wall clock away from the cabinet
lighting_and_materials: diffuse daylight and warm practical light
matte wood, woven fiber, and pale plaster
spec.task_setup: Keep the initial state task-ready but not complete: the cabinet starts closed, the target remains retrievable after opening, and no robot motion is baked into the scene
camera_readability: show the cabinet front, handles, robot aisle, and targets in one fixed main view
avoid handle occlusion and severe foreshortening
negative_constraints: mirrors, glass doors, reflective chrome, random clutter, intersecting doors or drawers

profiles.brief: A realistic non-robot living-room scene for rigid-body physics events.

activity_zones: a compact dining and object-interaction area

objects.name: solid rectangular dining table
objects.placement: beside the right window with clear edges and walking space

objects.name: ceramic fruit bowl
objects.placement: near its center without blocking the physics targets

objects.name: red rubber ball
objects.placement: inside the left table edge with a clear rolling route

objects.name: blue ceramic mug
objects.placement: upright near the far-right quadrant

objects.name: three-seat sofa
objects.placement: against the long left wall facing the media console

objects.name: low coffee table
objects.placement: centered on a woven rug in front of the sofa

objects.name: two armchairs and a floor lamp
objects.placement: across from the sofa with the lamp in the rear corner

wall_and_ceiling: a framed landscape print above the sofa
a pendant over the dining table
lighting_and_materials: soft window daylight with warm lamps
matte wood, woven textile, and neutral plaster
spec.task_setup: All movable objects begin stable and separately visible before the deterministic physics intervention
camera_readability: frame the dining table as the main action area while retaining living-room context
negative_constraints: glass tables, mirrors, excessive ornaments, printed text, floating or intersecting objects
